evals.prompt: Our e-commerce system currently has one shared Customer class used everywhere, carrying cart, wishlist, deliveryAddress, taxId, and creditTerms. The ordering, shipping, and billing teams keep stepping on each other whenever it changes. How should we restructure the Customer concept? Show the proposed model shape.
assertions: Recommends splitting the person into separate per-context models (e.g. Ordering's Customer, Shipping's Recipient, Billing's AccountHolder) rather than keeping one unified/canonical Customer type

States that each context's model carries only the fields it needs (e.g. Shipping's Recipient holds name/address/phone, Billing holds billing address/tax id/credit terms) and that they are translated at the boundary
Does NOT recommend unifying into one shared Customer type for DRY-ness

evals.prompt: Design the Order and Shipment part of our domain model. An Order has multiple order lines and results in a shipment. Right now everything hangs off a big Customer object that loads all of a customer's orders, lines, and shipments at once. Propose the aggregate design and explain how Order and Shipment relate.
assertions: Makes Order and Shipment separate aggregates (small aggregates) rather than one large aggregate containing everything
Has Order reference Shipment by identity/id rather than holding the Shipment object directly
States that cross-aggregate consistency between Order and Shipment is eventual (e.g. reached afterward via a domain event), not within one transaction

evals.prompt: We need to integrate with a third-party address/party service. Its client returns a PartyDTO. Show how our Shipping context should consume this so the vendor's types don't spread through our domain. Name the component and describe what it returns.
assertions: Introduces an anti-corruption layer / translator that returns our own domain type (e.g. Recipient) and never exposes PartyDTO past the layer
Describes translation in BOTH directions (not merely a thin forwarding client that returns the raw vendor DTO)

evals.prompt: Review this design: Order is a class with getLines() and setTotal(), and an OrderService.recalculate(order) computes and assigns the total. Is this a good domain model? If not, show a better shape.
assertions: Identifies this as the anemic domain model anti-pattern
Moves behaviour onto Order itself (e.g. Order.addLine recomputes the total internally) so the total-equals-sum-of-subtotals invariant cannot be violated from outside
